subject: Re: PII handling for Acme prompts/outputs
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (post-demo recap)

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed: 

• Scope: you asked about how Redwood handles PII that may be present in prompts and in model outputs (both hosted API and Dedicated options).
• Questions to confirm: what is stored by default, where data is stored (region), retention periods, logging access controls, and options for disabling or routing logs.

What I’m sending now: attached is a simple data-flow diagram (redwood_pii_data_flow_diagram.png) and a one-page SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf). Below are the high-level answers; Neha (security) and I will follow up with the exact contractual language and DPA link.

High-level answers:
- Hosted API (default): transient request processing with encrypted transit. By default we persist prompt + output records for up to 30 days for abuse detection, debugging, and quality monitoring. These records are access-controlled and encrypted at rest.
- Dedicated/Private: for Dedicated or Private deployments we can disable retention of prompt/output payloads entirely; logs can be configured to include only telemetry/metrics.
- Data residency: Hosted data is stored in the region you select (we support US and EU regions); Dedicated can be deployed inside your VPC/region.
- Controls: KMS-managed keys, role-based access control, audit logs, and SOC2 attestations.

Next steps we agreed: provide a written confirmation of retention and residency details, share the DPA, and, if acceptable, provide a 30-day test instance on Dedicated. I’ve looped in Neha to confirm retention windows and logging specifics inline.

Thanks again — I’ll flag the items Neha will add.

Best,
Nikhil
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Nikhil — useful recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop legal: 

1) When you say you persist prompt+output for up to 30 days, is that the default for all customers on the hosted offering? Can customers opt out of that retention without moving to Dedicated/Private?
2) Are raw prompts ever stored in long-term logs/backups outside the 30-day window? For compliance we need to be able to say raw user input is not retained beyond the stated period.
3) For EU data residency: if we select EU region, does everything (including logs, backups, and audit trails) remain in the EU?
4) Can you share the exact DPA clause language for prompt retention so our legal team can review?

Also please confirm who at Redwood has access to prompt-level data and what controls you have for privileged access.

—Sarah
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (post-demo recap)

Hi Sarah — answers inline and a few more specifics. Neha, adding any corrections.

1) Retention default and opt-out: Yes — for the Redwood hosted API the default retention for prompt+output payloads is 30 days. This retention is primarily for abuse detection, model quality troubleshooting, and customer support debugging. Customers can request reduced retention or opt out as part of an Enterprise contract/DPA. Opting out without Dedicated typically requires contractual terms (we remove prompt/output persistence for your tenant).

2) Backups and long-term logs: Raw prompts are not kept in long-term backups beyond the configured retention period. We isolate raw payload storage from long-term analytics datasets. Long-term analytics only retains aggregated telemetry (no raw prompt text) and is retained for 12 months by default.

3) EU residency: When you select the EU region for your tenant, data-at-rest for prompt/output payloads and primary logs remain in the EU region(s) we designate (we currently support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). Snapshots/backups for hosted accounts are also kept within the selected region unless otherwise contracted.

4) Access controls: Access to prompt-level data is limited to a small set of authorized engineers and support staff for debugging and abuse investigations. Access is audited via immutable audit logs and requires justification. All access is gated by RBAC and logged.

Related items and links: 
- DPA draft (shared link): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/ACME-DPA-v1.docx
- SOC2 summary: https://app.redwood.com/docs/soc2-summary

Neha — can you add the definitive retention values and confirm the logging metrics retention?

Thanks,
Nikhil
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs (post-demo recap)

Hi Sarah — adding the security/ops-level details you asked for. 

• Definitive retention numbers (hosted default): prompt+output payloads = 30 days (configurable by contract). Telemetry/metrics (aggregated) = 12 months. Audit logs (access/audit trails) = 24 months by default; can be included in export for audits.
• Backups/snapshots: for hosted EU tenants, backups remain within the EU region chosen; we do not replicate hosted customer raw payloads outside the chosen region.
• Privileged access: access to raw prompt payloads requires a support/security ticket and is logged. We use KMS for encryption at rest; for Enterprise we can support customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key).
• Deletion/DARs: we support data subject requests via our support portal; for cases that require record deletion we provide a deletion confirmation and an audit trail entry.

If you have a specific retention number or a compliance requirement (e.g., zero retention, or retention <7 days), please flag it and we’ll scope whether it can be accommodated in the hosted plan or if Dedicated/Private is required.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
